  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level fixed factor, using Mouse as a random effect or blocking factor to account for 8 mice contributing repeated measures",
    "For Success (binary: 0/1), use logistic regression or generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family and logit link, with Stim Paradigm as predictor and Mouse as random effect",
    "Given the large sample size (n=76655) and substantial group size imbalance (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), use Type III sums of squares and verify homogeneity of variance assumptions",
    "For Time-to-Target, consider log-transformation due to right skew (max=201.39, mean=2.81, sd=2.08) or use robust ANOVA alternatives",
    "Include Mouse as a random intercept in all models to account for inter-subject variability evident in summary_by_mouse_and_stim_paradigm.csv (e.g., SC11LM Sham success rate 0.067 vs SC11L1RF Sham 0.245)"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For significant ANOVA results, conduct pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms using estimated marginal means (emmeans)",
    "Apply Tukey's HSD for all pairwise comparisons of estimated marginal means from the linear mixed models",
    "For the binomial Success model, use pairwise odds ratio comparisons with z-tests on the logit scale",
    "Focus particular attention on Sham vs active stimulation conditions, and Combined vs unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only)",
    "Report confidence intervals for all pairwise differences to assess practical significance beyond statistical significance"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control familywise error rate across the 10 pairwise comparisons per response variable using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at α=0.05, applied separately within each of the 5 response variables; for simultaneous inference across all 5 variables, consider Bonferroni adjustment (α=0.01 per variable) or hierarchical testing with Success and Time-to-Target as primary endpoints",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Given that Stim Paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels and the goal is prediction of paradigm from performance variables, recommend a multinomial logistic regression or multinomial probit model with Stim Paradigm as response and the 5 performance variables as predictors. This is the appropriate categorical-response model rather than ordinary linear regression. Alternative: random forest or gradient boosting classifier given potential nonlinear relationships and interactions (e.g., Sham shows distinctly lower Success and higher Time-to-Target). Include Mouse as a grouping variable for cross-validation stratification. If interpretability is prioritized, use multinomial logistic regression with LASSO regularization to handle potential multicollinearity among predictors (Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target likely correlated).",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures within mice; address via mixed models with Mouse random effects",
    "Normality: Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency show extreme right skew (Path Efficiency max=29.8 vs mean=0.47); use log transformation or robust methods",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test across 5 groups for each variable; given large n, Welch's ANOVA as alternative",
    "Multicollinearity: Check VIF among predictors for predictive model; Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency expected to correlate negatively",
    "Complete separation check for multinomial model: Sham is well-separated on Success (0.27 vs 0.67-0.78 for others), which may cause convergence issues; use Firth's penalized likelihood or ridge penalty",
    "Model convergence: Verify for GLMM and multinomial models given large dataset and unbalanced design"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham will show significantly lower Success rates and higher Time-to-Target compared to all active stimulation conditions (Sham Success=0.273 vs Combined=0.780, Dim Visual=0.673, ICMS=0.685, Bright Visual=0.785)",
    "Combined stimulation will outperform unimodal conditions on Path Efficiency and Success, with mean Path Efficiency 0.502 vs Dim Visual 0.434 and ICMS 0.432",
    "Bright Visual Only will show similar or better performance to Combined on Success (0.785 vs 0.780) but may differ in Path Efficiency or AD",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only will be statistically similar to each other but inferior to Combined and Bright Visual Only",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will be highest for Combined and Bright Visual (0.399, 0.387), lowest for Sham (0.236), suggesting more exploratory or variable trajectories with effective stimulation",
    "Average Speed will be highest for Combined (12.83) and Bright Visual (12.68), lowest for Sham (10.74)"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe group imbalance: Combined represents 63.7% of data (48846/76655) vs Sham 4.6% (3505/76655), reducing power for Sham comparisons and potentially biasing variance estimates",
    "Missing trial-level information: No data on trial order, learning effects, or session structure; cannot assess whether performance differences reflect acute stimulation effects or learned strategies",
    "No baseline within-mouse Sham data for most mice: Cannot establish causal counterfactual; observed Sham performance may reflect different motivational states",
    "AD interpretation uncertain: Higher AD with stimulation could indicate more efficient exploration or less direct paths; without trajectory visualization, mechanistic interpretation limited",
    "Cross-sectional design within replication 2: Cannot assess test-retest reliability or stimulation order effects",
    "Binary Success may mask graded performance differences; continuous proximity-to-target measure would add sensitivity"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Bayesian multilevel multinomial logistic regression predicting Stim Paradigm from the 5 performance variables with Mouse as random effect, using weakly informative priors to regularize estimates given group imbalance; compute posterior probabilities of correct classification and conduct posterior predictive checks to assess model calibration.
